## Source 28
SCOPE. I read every note in public/data/voiced-teachings.json from 7034 to 7476: 443 notes from 34 videos. 235 are opening notes, 190 middlegame and 18 endgame; the student is White in 213 and Black in 230. The `concepts` field is empty on all 443 and `teaches` is filled on 99, so the teaching lives in the prose. I compared the slice with Reader 8's 98-entry catalogue, which covers this same range at a coarser grain (digests/teach.md, Source 8). Spot checks support that catalogue: moveFundamentals 'queen-off-file' (moveFundamentals.ts:65-68, :976) was built from note 7311 in this slice, and forkTrick.ts:126 trickSidestepped does sidestep the trick in 7302-7303. The list below has 59 entries. 46 are acts the coarse read missed or folded into a broader bucket. 13 are acts it already had, re-checked here with details or code facts specific to this slice. Everything is paraphrased. The reference coach's name is never written; the one service file named after him is written as [coach-name]Behaviors.ts.

THE MISSES THAT MATTER MOST (opening and traps first, per F02-F04):
(1) A trap taught with its conditions, plus the final safety check: queens facing each other, kings uncastled, their queen guarded only by its king. Only Review can see this: reviewTeachingPoints.ts:146-166 royalDefenderTarget, called at reviewFullData.ts:849. It also skips pawns (reviewTeachingPoints.ts:152), so 'f7 is guarded only by the king', the most-taught weak point in the opening, is never computed.
(2) A pattern's precondition disappears and the pattern is off. Only the centre-fork trick has this (forkTrick.ts:126). moveInsight.ts:668 greekGift fires only when the engine's best move IS the sacrifice. F04 needs a general tracker.
(3) Deflection without capturing the guard, either by a check or by forcing a recapture somewhere else. No such producer exists. detectRemovalOfGuard needs the guard itself captured (tacticClassifier.ts:457), and tacticsDetector.ts:293-300 suppresses a false skewer in note 7331's own game without adding a deflection read.
(4) Overload where the guard's second job is stopping mate. findOverloadedPieces counts only two attacked pieces worth at least 3 (tacticsDetector.ts:699, :711).
(5) Their move opens a line for your piece, or spends their own blocking resource. theirMoveCost has exactly four kinds (theirMoveCost.ts:23). Its 'hole' kind only fires when a student KNIGHT reaches the square within two jumps (theirMoveCost.ts:35, :82-83), so 'their pawn push gives your bishop c5' (7055-7056) is never said.
(6) A clamp built up over several moves, with the running count. moveIntent's PREVENTS needs the stopped move to be worth at least 100cp (moveIntent.ts:71, :165), so a positional clamp on a freeing push usually stays silent.
(7) Castling denial, in both directions. castleIsOneMoveAway checks attacked transit squares (positionalRead.ts:156-165). castleRoute does not (kingSafety.ts:202-215), yet detectCentralKingDanger (kingSafety.ts:159) and [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:298 build 'get castled' advice on it. That is a latent D10 risk; I read it but did not run it.
(8) Self-interference: a natural move blocks your own piece's line (4 notes). Nothing produces it.
(9) Future scope: judge a piece by the line it will have after your planned pawn moves (3 notes). Nothing produces it.
(10) Your move leaves them one defence, and it is ugly. walkForcedSequence (onlyMoveSequence.ts:57) could walk the forced line but has no production caller (G8.5).

REACH GAPS (S1/F2). Several existing computers reach only one surface:
- speedRunReads runs only on the student's turn (thinkAloud.ts:257).
- autopilotRecapture runs only from PuzzleBoard.tsx:652.
- pieceOptions runs only from chat (coachService.ts:1483).
- sacrificeCompensation runs only in Review (reviewFullData.ts:915, coachFeatureService.ts:2750).
- The opening lecture's 'more testing try' line exists only in Review (reviewOpeningTheory.ts:691-700).
- [coach-name]Behaviors' 'down material' rule runs only in Learn (CoachTeachPage.tsx:293).

CORPUS DEFECTS, checked on the board with chess.js:
- D10: 7287-7288 say Qa4 forks and wins the queen. After 11...Qxd7 12.Qa4 the pinned queen simply plays 12...Qxa4, so it is a queen trade.
- V16: 7286 tells the White student 'when you're down material', but White is up a piece (material 37 to 35). Its advice that trading helps the side that is down also contradicts the app's own rule at [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:576-577. The seat guard cannot catch this, because the note's seat does match.

RULE FLAGS in the slice:
- V1 first person, 18 notes: 7087 7169 7171 7172 7184 7211 7221 7224 7225 7232 7233 7263 7290 7394 7408 7409 7417 7465.
- V1 'let's / we', 4 notes: 7065 7257 7311 7366.
- V8 and F10, ratings and counts, 6 notes: 7052 7053 7065 7211 7288 7394.
- F05, questions to the audience: 7124 and 7174.
- S12: 7181 warns about an unsound sacrifice in advance.
- F0b, a verdict with no reason: 7087 and 7465.
- F0d, borderline: 7142 uses a living player's first name as an opening nickname.
Opening names that come from people (Najdorf, Maroczy, Smyslov) are fine.
RHYTHM: Measured over notes 7034-7476. These are distilled paraphrases, so absolute word counts run below the raw speech.

PER NOTE. The median is 18 words in the opening (235 notes) and 18 in the middlegame (190). The 18 endgame notes have a median of 22. The 90th percentile is 39 words in the opening, 44 in the middlegame and 39 in the endgame. 93 notes (21%) are 8 words or fewer, bare move calls such as 'Black castles'. 41% of notes follow the OPPONENT's move, so he diagnoses their choice almost as often as he guides the student's.

TWO REGIMES (the key finding). In game-commentary videos he notes 77-100% of the plies, at 12-19 words each, and up to about a third are bare. In lesson videos he notes only 27-47% of the plies, at 37-47 words each, with no bare notes at all. Both spend roughly 10-28 words per ply. The budget is about the same; the distribution is not. Lessons skip the routine plies and pool the words where the idea lives. For the decider, that means pooling the words at decision moments rather than spreading them evenly.

LONG NOTES. The 8 longest notes (60-89 words: 7038, 7096, 7150, 7156, 7161, 7218, 7224, 7282) all sit at a decision point:
- a false alarm with its capture branches;
- an attack window;
- a trap with its conditions;
- a queen post, with their best and their instinctive reply;
- a dead break that becomes a wing plan;
- the wrong ways to break a pin;
- development against material;
- an attack plan with its prerequisites.

ORDER inside a long note: flag the moment, then the condition or why now, then each tempting or popular wrong option with its refutation, then the move and its jobs, then the line or consequence, and the habit or principle last. Opponent-move notes run in a different order: their move plus a verdict, then the board reason, then what it hands you or how to punish it. Their GOOD moves get credit plus the drawback to exploit (7410-7411).

TWO-PLY PATTERN. He states the problem on THEIR move ('their knight now hits e5') and gives the answer on the STUDENT's move ('defend a pawn with a pawn', 7124-7125). That maps to Learn's held move, not to an F05 question.

BY PHASE. The opening carries naming, the opening's ideas as a list, theory status, verdicts on their moves, traps with their conditions and move order. Quiet middlegames carry clamps, plans by destination and prophylaxis. Critical moments carry candidates, the failing tempting move, the line and a safety check (no in-between check). After winning material he consolidates and chooses between attacking and trading. Endgames get short technique and conversion lines.
- [NEW] Overload where the guard's second job is stopping mate: both answers lose (Middlegame, right after a forcing capture with check) e.g. A bishop check makes their queen choose. If it takes back, the rook it was guarding falls; if it stays put, it is mate. Name both branches, then the verdict. -> PARTIAL. tacticsDetector.ts:690-723 findOverloadedPieces needs two attacked pieces worth at least 3 (:699, :711). A guard whose other duty is a mating square is never found, so the mate-duty case is MISSING.
- [NEW] Deflection without capturing the guard, by a check or by forcing a recapture elsewhere (Tactics against a sole defender, middlegame or endgame) e.g. Their queen is the only guard of the corner rook, so a bishop check drives it off. Later a rook trade forces their queen off e8, and the knight it guarded on e6 is left hanging. -> MISSING. tacticClassifier.ts:457 detectRemovalOfGuard needs the guard itself captured, and tacticsDetector.ts:651 skips king guards. tacticsDetector.ts:293-300 suppresses a false skewer in note 7331's own game (the comment calls it a deflection) but adds no deflection producer. 'deflection' exists only as a puzzle-theme label (tacticClassifierService.ts:23, :47).
- [NEW] Their move opens a line for your piece and uses up the pawn move that could have closed it (Right after an opponent's opening pawn move) e.g. Their early central pawn push opens your bishop's diagonal toward f2. It also spends the pawn that could have stepped to e3 to block that diagonal. -> PARTIAL. theirMoveCost.ts:23 has four kinds only (hole, bishop-shut, castling, structure); 'opens a line for your piece' and 'spent a defensive resource' are not among them.
- [NEW] A new hole taken by a bishop or any other piece, not only a knight (Right after an opponent's pawn advance) e.g. Their pawn steps past c5, so your dark-squared bishop drops straight into that square, with d6 and c6 to follow. -> PARTIAL. theirMoveCost.ts:35 and :82-83 name a new hole only when a student KNIGHT reaches it within two jumps; moveInsight.ts:1102 holeAccess is knight-only too. A hole the bishop takes is never said.
- [NEW] Your move leaves them one defence, and it is an ugly one (After the student's forcing or probing move) e.g. A knight jump at f2 looks shallow, but their only way to hold is a knight to the rim. Later, a knight on c7 sets a problem they can only solve with a run of precise moves. -> MISSING for the opponent's side. criticalMoment.ts:150-153 counts only-moves for the student. onlyMoveSequence.ts:57 walkForcedSequence could walk the line but has no production caller. coachFeatureService.ts:1175 only credits 'their only move' in Review.
- [NEW] A clamp on the square they need, built up over several moves, with the running count (Quiet middlegame plan against a square the opponent needs) e.g. The bishop to f4 covers d6, the e5 push squeezes it, and the knight to e4 adds another piece on it. Then say how much control is now on that square. -> PARTIAL. moveIntent.ts:383-410 stopReason counts 'you cover X three times to their one', but only after PREVENTS fires. That needs the stopped move to be worth at least 100cp (moveIntent.ts:71, :165), which a positional freeing push rarely is. Nothing keeps the tally across moves.
- [NEW] Level but comfortable: which side is being set the problems (Assessment at the end of the opening) e.g. Once the bishop is anchored the game is level, but their moves set you no problems, and their natural bishop sortie would already lose to a check on f2. -> PARTIAL. speedRunReads.ts:68-79 anyMoveFine reads only the student's ease: their top three moves within a small gap, and only from move 8 (:70, :74). Nothing compares how many good moves each side has.
- [NEW] Proportional response: meet a passive slip with plain development (Opponent's slow or passive opening move) e.g. Their rook-pawn move only lets the pawn be won back and wastes time. There is no need to hunt for a refutation; just develop. Nothing fancy is needed against a harmless sideline, and you play solidly once a pawn up. -> MISSING as a framing. The nearest is speedRunReads.ts:68 anyMoveFine.
- [NEW] Size their concession honestly: what it does NOT give you, and what it does (An opponent's early exchange, or the student's own check) e.g. Their capture on d4 doesn't hand you the whole centre, because they can still hit back in the middle, but it frees c3 for your knight for nothing. Your bishop check looks as if it wins the queen, but it doesn't, because a knight can block. -> MISSING. theirMoveCost.ts:60 names only positive costs. bluffDetector.ts:37 covers their empty threats, not the student overrating their own move.
- [NEW] Their setup contradicts its own plan (The opponent leaves the plan their opening announced) e.g. An early f-pawn push belongs with long castling and a pawn storm. Castling short behind it only weakens them a little, so it isn't dangerous. -> MISSING. mastersPlanRead.ts:83 knows which side masters castle to; ruleException.ts:70 checks the f/g-pawn rule for the student only.
- [NEW] The usual square for a piece in this pawn structure (Development choices in a named structure) e.g. In this ...e5 Sicilian structure the queen's knight goes to d7, almost never c6. The knight's main post later is e5. -> PARTIAL. mastersPlanRead.ts:143-144 records placements only for queens, rooks, or pieces that reach the 4th/5th rank, at most one per side, so a back-rank development choice never registers.
- [NEW] Luft made with a pawn that also does a second job (Late middlegame or endgame, back-rank safety) e.g. In the ending, air for the king doesn't have to come from the rook pawn. A different pawn push gives the king room, stops a rook raid and prepares to anchor a piece. -> PARTIAL. moveFundamentals.ts:766-787 calls a move luft only if it is a one-square push to the third rank on the shield files, with the king on its castled square (:777). The game's next move, the two-square push 20.g4, never counts as luft, and nothing compares the luft candidates.
- [NEW] Which rook goes to the open file (Conversion, taking a file) e.g. When converting, put the rook on the open file that doesn't leave its partner buried behind it. -> MISSING as a computed choice. It exists only as prose at principleVoice.ts:76, and phaseTransitionDetector.ts:114 rooksConnected is a yes/no.
- [NEW] Self-interference: the natural move blocks your own piece's line (Choosing a development, block or retreat square) e.g. Their instinctive bishop move to d2 cuts their own queen off from the d4 pawn. Your knight retreats to e3, not g2, where it would bury the bishop. Your bishop goes to b2, not d2, where a pawn push would deflect it and force your king to move. -> MISSING. refutedAlternativeCore.ts:63 droppedJob only covers a job the MOVED piece gives up. Nothing reads 'this move blocks another of your own pieces'.
- [NEW] A square valued for its safety and its onward routes, not its activity now (Quiet piece placement) e.g. The queen's square on the a-file isn't special in itself. Nothing can easily hit it there, it is out of the other pieces' way, and from it the queen can swing to b4 or drop back. -> MISSING. pieceOptions.ts:62-75 gives a piece's duties and options (chat only, coachService.ts:1483), and forwardTeaching.ts:186/236 finds a route to a target. Nothing scores a square by safety plus onward routes.
- [NEW] Future scope: judge a piece by the line it gets after your planned pawn moves (Development choices and structural judgement) e.g. The bishop on b2 looks dead now, but the c4 and d5 pushes you plan will open it. The 'passive' e7 bishop is the piece that backs your c5 break. A bad bishop guards good pawns and wakes up once its pawn advances. -> MISSING. positionReadingService.ts:508/556 marks a bishop bad from the current board only, and principleAttribution.ts:1292-1302 says to trade it. Nothing reads the scope after the student's planned breaks.
- [NEW] Keep the bishop that matches your weak pawn's colour (Choosing between saving a piece and keeping a bishop) e.g. Don't save the knight by dropping the dark-squared bishop back to d2. That bishop is the one that will guard your dark-square d4 pawn from e3 later. -> MISSING. tradeJudgement.ts:40 judges trades by the engine's piece table and cpLoss. The bad-bishop logic has no inverse that says 'this bishop guards your pawns' colour'.
- [NEW] When forced back, retreat to the square that still does something (An attacked piece has to retreat) e.g. When the rook on b7 is hit, don't just drop to the first rank. Taking a7 first would be fine, and stepping back to b3 keeps the rook ready to swing toward their king. -> PARTIAL. moveFundamentals 'keep-working' (doc :54-55, ids :900/:926) covers only a piece kicked by a PAWN that steps to a square where it still works. A capture on the way out is never proposed.
- [NEW] Skip the automatic recapture and take something bigger first, said when the student finds it (Middlegame, in the middle of an exchange) e.g. There is no need to take back the knight. The queen grabs on b2, and the corner rook is the real prize. -> PARTIAL. kneeJerk.ts:15-22 and moveInsight.ts:642 autopilotRecapture only diagnose the miss (at least 100cp, after the student has already recaptured), and autopilotRecapture is reached only from PuzzleBoard.tsx:652. thinkAloud.ts:145 notYet is the live 'first this' voice.
- [NEW] Don't grab: the piece that recaptures or replaces it ends up better placed (A tempting capture in a tense position) e.g. Taking their bishop lets their queen land on b6, where it is hard to move. Taking the e5 knight lets their recapture pile pressure on you, so kick it instead. -> PARTIAL. recaptureChoice.ts:56/103 judges the student's own recapture, and tradeJudgement.ts:40 judges the trade. Neither reads 'their recapturing piece lands somewhere better'.
- [NEW] Your extra guard decides which piece they can recapture with (Exchanges on a contested square) e.g. With your bishop now guarding d5, their queen can't take there. Only the knight can, and that recapture is their mistake. -> PARTIAL. The pin-aware exchange count (positionReadingService.ts:1257-1268) proves it, but nothing says 'your guard forces the worse recapture'.
- [SEEN, confirmed twice] A pin's real job: it takes a defender out of the count (Right after a pin appears) e.g. Their bishop pins your knight, so your d5 pawn has lost a guard and you add one. Their pin on your c3 knight is what makes the threat on e4 real. -> PARTIAL. The exchange count is pin-aware (positionReadingService.ts:1257-1268, causalChain.ts:32-42), so the threat itself is computed. But causalChain's relation types (causalChain.ts:62-70) have no pin-removes-a-defender link, and pinPressure.ts:82/147 only says 'break the pin or add a defender'.
- [NEW] A pattern's condition just vanished, so the pattern is off (After a trade or a prophylactic move changes a pattern's conditions) e.g. With their knight traded away, the bishop sacrifice on h7 no longer works, so keeping your bishop aimed at their castled king costs nothing. After your bishop steps back to b3, their fork trick no longer works either. The reference never names that trick; the app can. -> PARTIAL. forkTrick.ts:126 trickSidestepped does this, for either side (forkTrick.ts:18-21), but only for the centre-fork trick. moveInsight.ts:668 greekGift fires only when the engine's best move IS the sacrifice. There is no condition tracker for named sacrifice patterns (F04).
- [NEW] Play out a pattern that fails here, to show the defender's resources (A demonstration inside a lesson) e.g. The bishop sacrifice on h2 is named as wrong for this position, then played through: the knight check, the queen heading for h2, and the defensive resources that make it less simple than it looks. -> PARTIAL. moveInsight.ts:668 greekGift explains a sacrifice only when it works. reviewSacrifice.ts:44 sacrificeCompensation is Review-only (reviewFullData.ts:915, coachFeatureService.ts:2750). Under RULEBOOK S12, Learn waits until the student actually plays an unsound sacrifice.
- [NEW] What a sacrifice still gains if it is declined (At a sacrifice) e.g. The bishop takes on h3. If they take it, a knight check forks king and queen. If they don't, the fianchetto bishop holding their centre is gone anyway. -> MISSING on live surfaces. speedRunReads.ts:383 goodInEveryBranch is for quiet moves. reviewSacrifice.ts:44 is Review-only and reads the eval, not the declined branch.
- [NEW] An attacked piece: invest it rather than save it (King attack) e.g. Instead of moving the attacked knight, sacrifice it on g6 to tear the h-file open. -> PARTIAL. kingAttack.ts:71 reads that a file opened or a shelter pawn was taken, but nothing frames the choice 'retreat it or invest it'.
- [NEW] Material against speed: ignore your loose pawn when mate is faster, take free material when it costs nothing (Decisions during an attack) e.g. Don't worry about the loose pawn: you are going for mate, and every move they spend taking it is a move not spent defending. Later, a free pawn on g7 is worth taking even in the middle of the attack. -> PARTIAL. moveInsight.ts:993 materialPlan and safetyHabits.ts:54 keepPressing exist, but nothing compares the tempo cost of their grab with the speed of your attack.
- [NEW] What an attack needs first, and when to strike (Planning a king attack) e.g. Open the centre before you sacrifice. Connect the rooks with a queen move that keeps the f-rook home for the break. Strike once their queen leaves the defence; two rooks and the queen are enough. -> PARTIAL. kingAttack.ts:71 and countKingAttack (kingSafety.ts:297) count the forces, and moveInsight.ts:573 theirMoveChanged reports what their move stopped guarding. Nothing triggers 'wait for the defender to leave, then strike'.
- [NEW] Put the heavy piece behind the break before you push (Preparing a flank break) e.g. Castle first so a rook stands behind the f-pawn, then push f5. -> PARTIAL. moveFundamentals.ts:999 'prepare-break' covers pawn moves only, and :1046 'rook-behind-pawn' covers a central pawn on a closed file. Castling to put a rook behind a flank break is not recognised.
- [NEW] Two good moves: the clinical one or the one that sets them more problems (Decision points with several good options) e.g. Giving up the exchange on a3 is strong, but the rook move sets them more problems. A quiet queen move holds everything, but developing and offering the knight is chosen instead. -> PARTIAL. reviewOpeningTheory.ts:691-700 says the engine prefers 'a sharper, more testing try', but only in Review's opening lecture. MISSING on live surfaces; it could be computed as how many good replies they have after each candidate.
- [NEW] Pick between candidate moves by which one uses their weaknesses (Middlegame choice) e.g. Their f-pawn left holes, so the knight jump into e3 beats the queen move. -> PARTIAL. moveInsight.ts:459 mechanismContrast compares two moves only by double attack, and deliberation.ts:144 weighs candidates by engine value.
- [NEW] Deny castling: your pieces cover the squares their king must cross (The opponent's king has not castled yet) e.g. The bishop on c5 stops them castling short. Once the knights join, their king can't castle on either side and is stuck in the middle. -> MISSING in both directions. positionalRead.ts:147-165 castleIsOneMoveAway checks attacked transit squares, but only as one yes/no answer for one side. kingSafety.ts:202-215 castleRoute ignores attacked squares, and detectCentralKingDanger (kingSafety.ts:159) and [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:298 build 'get castled' advice on it.
- [NEW] A two-step threat, and the developing move that takes the sting out (Sharp openings with a weakened diagonal) e.g. They threaten to take on e4 and follow with a queen check on h4. The knight to c3 guards e4 while developing, and after it the check is met by g3. -> PARTIAL. opponentIntent.ts:55 gives their idea and your answer, branched; latentDanger.ts:87 also helps. speedRunReads.ts:400 takeTheSting runs on the student's turn only (thinkAloud.ts:257).
- [NEW] Exploit the drawback of their GOOD move (The opponent plays a strong move) e.g. Their bishop to b5 is one of the best moves, but your queenside knight can hit it, so the knight heads to a6 and then c7. -> PARTIAL. theirMoveCost.ts:60 covers structural costs only, and moveInsight.ts:523 weakenedBy covers weakened squares. 'Their piece is now a target' is not one of the cost kinds.
- [NEW] Breaking a pin brings a threat back (Breaking a pin) e.g. The queen steps off the pinned line, and the knight's capture on b5 is a threat again. -> PARTIAL. reviewMoveTeaching.ts:202-213 unpinPoint (Review) and playCommentary.ts:914-918 (Learn) describe the unpin, but the renewed threat is never linked to it.
- [NEW] The structure's built-in hole and the usual piece that covers it (The move that sets the opening's structure) e.g. Every ...e5 Sicilian of this kind has to watch d5, so the bishop goes to e6, guarding it and keeping their bishop off c4. -> PARTIAL. concessionBeat.ts:360 findStudentDrawback names the drawback, but nothing names the standard fix.
- [NEW] A tempo is worth more when the game turns on a development lead (Opening with a development lead) e.g. The bishop check is exact because their natural block isn't available. If they block with the bishop, taking it wins another tempo, and in this kind of position each tempo counts double. -> PARTIAL. tempoCount.ts:7-9 counts a piece's third move, and speedRunReads.ts:244 awkwardBlock reads a forced awkward block. Nothing raises a tempo's stakes when the game is about a development lead.
- [NEW] A break that can never happen means a new plan (Cramped structures) e.g. In this bind the central d5 break will never come, so you chip at the wing with a6 and b5 against c4 and settle into a long manoeuvring game. -> PARTIAL. mastersPlanRead.ts:83 lists the breaks (Learn only), but nothing reasons 'this break can't happen, so play this instead'.
- [NEW] Their sideline doesn't change your plan (The opponent deviates without making a threat) e.g. The early bishop pin is a sideline. Keep your usual setup. -> PARTIAL. falseAlarm.ts:37 covers a real threat you can ignore; a harmless deviation has no read.
- [NEW] A plan that depends on where they put a piece (Early opening against an offbeat setup) e.g. Expand with e6 and d5, or fianchetto instead, depending on where their queen settles. Against a quiet bishop move, don't lock yourself into one system: stay flexible. -> PARTIAL. opponentIntent.ts:55 gives branched answers to their idea.
- [NEW] Correct the obvious misreading of a move's target (Attacking sequences) e.g. The queen to h5 is not after the bishop; it is heading for h2. -> PARTIAL. moveIntent.ts:124 gives engine-proven prepares and prevents, but there is no 'this is not about X' clause.
- [NEW] Say what a finished sequence achieved (After an exchange sequence) e.g. That trade did two things: it freed your long-diagonal bishop and loosened their hold on the centre. -> PARTIAL. positionFacts.ts:908 phaseVerdictLine sums up the position, but there is no before-and-after diff for one sequence.
- [NEW] An imprecision the position forgave, and why (The student's slight inaccuracy) e.g. Jumping the knight in was a little hasty, but their passivity let you get away with it, and stepping back is fine. -> PARTIAL. accuracyService.ts:122 gradeMove gives the grade (G9), but there is no 'it cost nothing because...' reason.
- [NEW] A defensive move named as correct, not timid (After the opponent increases pressure) e.g. Adding a guard to d5 with the bishop isn't passive. In these openings you sometimes simply have to defend, and it is sound. -> PARTIAL. speedRunReads.ts:82 uglyButRight only covers a best move that doubles your pawns or walks a piece back home.
- [NEW] Mirror comparison (Offbeat setups) e.g. The queenside pawn fianchetto is playable; the same pawn moves on the kingside would wreck the king's shelter. -> MISSING. ruleException.ts:70 knows the f/g-pawn rule only for a king that has castled.
- [NEW] The worse side keeps fighting (Worse or lost positions) e.g. A pawn for a piece is not the end: the side that is ahead still has to convert. Keep making threats, and remember that a desperate grab in a lost position only loses more. -> PARTIAL. [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:576-577 says 'down material: don't trade, look for activity', but it is used in Learn only (imported at CoachTeachPage.tsx:293).
- [NEW] A capture chosen to close lines toward your own king (Opening, with your own king exposed) e.g. After the sharp f-pawn thrust, recapturing on e4 with that pawn lowers the risk of your king being opened up. -> MISSING. kingSafety.ts:56 detectKingExposure reads exposure, but nothing explains a capture as closing a line.
- [NEW] Knowledge: a check that also hits a piece can be answered by that piece blocking (Tactics around checks) e.g. Their knight takes on d4 and the queen check looks like a fork, but the knight just drops back to c6 and blocks. So take the knight first, and then the check picks up the bishop. -> PARTIAL. checkMethod.ts:32 teaches the three ways to meet a check, and thinkAloud.ts:145 notYet says 'take the knight first'. Neither names the forked piece blocking as the reason the check fails.
- [SEEN, refined] A trap taught with its trigger conditions and the last safety check (An opening trap set by a developing move) e.g. Queens face each other, kings are uncastled, and their queen is guarded only by its king. Develop the bishop to c4; if they capture, the check on f7 drags the king away and the queen falls. Before cashing in, confirm no in-between check saves them; here their own pawn blocks it. -> PARTIAL. reviewTeachingPoints.ts:146-166 royalDefenderTarget is Review-only (reviewFullData.ts:849). There is no live trap computer for the pattern's conditions (F04), and no in-between-check habit in safetyHabits.ts.
- [SEEN, refined] The opponent's known slip, punished without fear, and the sacrifice they hope for is bad for them (The opponent leaves book with a popular slip) e.g. The early bishop to c5 is a known inaccuracy, so take the centre pawn. The bishop check on f2 that people dread actually loses for them, and retreating the bishop gives up the pawn for nothing. -> refutedAlternativeCore.ts:159/219, forkTrick.ts:81 and bluffDetector.ts:37.
- [SEEN, refined] f7 and f2 as the opening's soft spot (Opening, against passive development) e.g. In the opening, link any fast assault with f7, the one weak point within reach. A knight jump toward f2 is the same idea from the other side. -> PARTIAL. keySquares.ts:97 keyTargetSquares names f7 as a target beside the king. But royalDefenderTarget skips pawns (reviewTeachingPoints.ts:152), so 'only the king guards f7' is never said.
- [SEEN, refined] A centralised piece with no support is a target: combine it with another weakness (Opening, after an opponent's pawn grab) e.g. Their knight in the centre has nothing behind it. Ignore it and hit f7: the pressure there plus the loose knight sets up a double attack. -> loosePieces.ts:35 findLoosePieces, moveInsight.ts:83 doubleAttack and latentFork.ts:161.
- [SEEN] Several wrong ways first, each with its refutation, then the clean move (Decision points in the opening) e.g. Against the pin, pushing the f-pawn weakens your king, and the counter-pin with the bishop gets kicked so the e4 pawn drops. So simply develop to d3. -> refutedAlternativeCore.ts:159 candidatesFromAmateur (what players at the student's level play) and deliberation.ts:144 (engine candidates).
- [SEEN, this slice] The opening's ideas, given as a list (First moves of a named opening) e.g. This defence has two ideas: a solid claim on d5 backed by e6, and quick kingside development without passive pieces. -> PARTIAL. openingIdentity.ts:85 openingIdentityLine covers what the opening provokes, gambits, aims and sharpness, but not a list of its ideas.
- [SEEN] What a gambit's material bought, and how to defuse it (Gambits) e.g. The pawn bought a lead in development. Against an unfamiliar gambit, develop, leave their advanced knight alone, and remember you can give the pawn back to reach an ending. -> PARTIAL. openingIdentity.ts:85 states the gambit fact, and sacrificeCompensation (reviewSacrifice.ts:44) is Review-only.
- [SEEN] One move, several jobs (Quiet moves with more than one purpose) e.g. The queen steps to e1 instead of pushing e5 at once: it avoids the queen trade and heads for an attacking post. -> moveIntent.ts:124 (prevents plus prepares). moveFundamentals.ts:65-68/:976 'queen-off-file' was written from note 7311 in this slice.
- [SEEN] Kick a piece with a pawn and gain time (The opponent has an advanced piece) e.g. Push the pawn at the annoying knight so it has to go back. -> moveFundamentals.ts:369-391 'tempo'.
- [SEEN] Call back to the earlier preparation (When an earlier move pays off) e.g. Good thing the bishop went back to b3 earlier. The whole point of the earlier pawn move was to make sure the rook could lift. -> causalChain.ts:639 buildCausalChain, planArc.ts:236 stepArc and motifLedger.ts:31 transferClause.
- [SEEN] Plan by destination (Manoeuvring) e.g. Think about where the knight is going: g5 in two moves, hitting h7 and e6. -> forwardTeaching.ts:186 computePieceRoute and :236 computeSliderRoute.
- [SEEN] Converting when ahead (After winning material) e.g. A piece up, finish development and defend, with no need to give anything back. Keeping the queens on is fine, and a rook lift toward their king may be the fastest win. -> conversionMethod.ts:44 readConversion.
